definitions.explanation: An official award given by the government in recognition of distinguished service or achievement. Also used figuratively for something one is proud of, like a badge of honor.

examples.japanese: {勲章|くんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}かった→授かる：12797_sazukaru⟧。
⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{勲章|くんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather received a medal in the war.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{傷|きず}→傷：02201_kizu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{勇気|ゆうき}→勇気：02499_yuuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{勲章|くんしょう}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われた→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: I was told that the scar was a badge of courage.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{功績|こうせき}→功績：04143_kouseki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{認|みと}められ→認める：02429_mitomeru⟧、⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧{勲章|くんしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{贈|おく}られた→贈る：09862_okuru⟧。
examples.english: In recognition of years of achievement, the Order of Culture was bestowed.

notes:
Refers to official government decorations awarded for distinguished service, as well as the figurative sense of a "badge of honor" — something one wears proudly as proof of effort or experience.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {勲章|くんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{授|さず}かる→授かる：12797_sazukaru⟧: to receive a decoration
- {勲章|くんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}る→贈る：09862_okuru⟧: to bestow a decoration
- ⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧{勲章|くんしょう}: Order of Culture (Japan's highest cultural award)
- {勲章|くんしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧につける: to wear a medal on one's chest

JAPAN'S DECORATION SYSTEM:
Japan awards decorations through the ⟦{叙勲|じょくん}→叙勲：25009_jokun⟧ system, typically to those who have contributed to society. Major categories include:
- {旭日章|きょくじつしょう}: Order of the Rising Sun
- {瑞宝章|ずいほうしょう}: Order of the Sacred Treasure
- ⟦{文化勲章|ぶんかくんしょう}→文化勲章：24796_bunkakunshou⟧: Order of Culture

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦メダル→メダル：10162_medaru⟧: medal — used for sports and competitions
- {褒章|ほうしょう}: medal of honor — awarded for specific acts of public service or moral courage
